sourcePaperRecords.title: Incidence hypergraphs: The categorical inconsistency of set-systems and a characterization of quiver exponentials
sourcePaperRecords.sourceVersion: arXiv:1805.07670v2, 2019-05-03, original manuscript PDF (different PDF numbering from final journal)
originalMathLocators: PDF index 16 (printed p17) §3.1 Definition 3.1.1: incidence presheaf category R=Set^D for shape D: 2→0 and 2→1; G=(V,E,I,s:I→V,t:I→E).
PDF index 18 (printed p19) §3.3 Definition 3.3.1: set-system-to-incidence functor I with incidences {(v,e):v∈ε(e)}; Lemma 3.3.2 this functor preserves neither limits nor colimits.

exactMathematicalFragment.objects: Three separate sets: vertices V, edge occurrences E and incidences I; two endpoint maps s:I→V and t:I→E.
exactMathematicalFragment.morphisms: Commuting triples (fV,fE,fI) with s'∘fI=fV∘s and t'∘fI=fE∘t
exactMathematicalFragment.equivalence: Componentwise bijective maps preserving incidence; ambient category functor/presheaf topos
exactMathematicalFragment.composition: componentwise composition of incidence-preserving maps; topoi support limits, colimits, subobject classifiers, exponentials
exactMathematicalFragment.mathPrerequisites: No imposed binary node bit, hyperedge rank, scheduler, field or physical metric. Functor category includes more general incidence objects than finite source rank-k set-system hypergraphs.

sourcePaperRecords.broadPhysicalCategory: Foundations of hypergraph/graph representation, no independently claimed gravitational or photon physics.
sourcePaperRecords.fineInterpretationBoundary: Source's ambient presheaf topos NOT the finite fixed-rank typed-with-Hamming-guard native Causal Step restricted subcategory. Lemma 3.3.2 directly prevents silently transporting all topos limits/colimits through naïve set-system encoding.
sourcePaperRecords.candidateNativeMapping: Frozen native historical V_t,E_t plus unique (e,v)∈I_t for each membership, with componentwise time-indexed inclusion maps; attributes retained separately. Injective incidence representation under original rank/unique-member restriction.
sourcePaperRecords.mappingStatus: exact structural representation and verified evolved inclusion on chosen histories; not full physical/process equivalence

sourcePaperRecords.title: Functorial Approach to Graph and Hypergraph Theory
sourcePaperRecords.sourceVersion: arXiv:1907.02574v1 2019-07-04 (author manuscript 106-page PDF, printed chapter page 15 at zero-index 14)
originalMathLocators: Original PDF index 14 (printed p15) Chapter 1 §1.1 Definition 1: right M-set X and monoid M, category G_(X,M) has objects V,A; hom(V,A)=X; hom(A,A)=M, composition by action; presheaf category [G_(X,M)^op,Set].
Source Introduction/Sections I–II: choices of X and M determine arity/orientation/symmetry of generalized graph objects, with exceptional loose/unfixed edges and morphism constraints.

exactMathematicalFragment.objects: Specified monoid M, right M-set X, two-object syntax category with graph-object data as contravariant Set-valued functor.
exactMathematicalFragment.morphisms: Natural transformations of presheaves; M action controls edge symmetries and X indexes endpoint/port incidences
exactMathematicalFragment.equivalence: Presheaf isomorphism under chosen (X,M); switching M or X is change of graph theory, not automatic equivalence
exactMathematicalFragment.composition: natural transformation and M-action composition; categorical (co)limits depend on full presheaf setting
exactMathematicalFragment.mathPrerequisites: Choice of graph arity X and symmetry monoid M, plus possible loose edges/extra morphisms; no physical time metric

sourcePaperRecords.broadPhysicalCategory: Generalized graph/hypergraph mathematical foundations; no physical force category assigned.
sourcePaperRecords.fineInterpretationBoundary: A fixed source rank k, unordered incidence occurrence may fit X of size k modulo S_k, but distinct repeated incidences/non-fixed edges can violate a naive endpoint tuple presentation. Need an exact functor and proof rather than presume equivalence.
sourcePaperRecords.candidateNativeMapping: Rank-k historical occurrence with k distinct incident nodes as symmetric k-tuple modulo S_k, only within chosen subcategory; verify whether full presheaf morphisms remain valid after imposed source restrictions.
sourcePaperRecords.mappingStatus: possible scoped representation, exact functor/reconstruction not yet proved

sourcePaperRecords.title: Adhesive Categories
sourcePaperRecords.sourceVersion: BRICS Research Series RS-03-31 October 2003 original author technical report; separate publication from 2005 'Adhesive and quasiadhesive categories' already indexed under LS/LS-009
originalMathLocators: PDF index 8, original printed p7 Definition 3.1: adhesive category has pullbacks, pushouts along monomorphisms and van Kampen squares.
PDF index 8, Counterexample 3.3: Pos, Cat, Top, Gpd are NOT adhesive.
PDF index 9, Proposition 3.4(iii): functor category [X,C] adhesive when C adhesive; Proposition 3.5 any elementary topos adhesive.
PDF index 14, Definition 5.1: double-pushout rule span L←K→R.

exactMathematicalFragment.objects: Ambient adhesive category C, monomorphisms and pullback/pushout diagrams, typed rewrite objects L,K,R.
exactMathematicalFragment.morphisms: Valid matches m:L→G, pushout complements and pushout gluing; side conditions needed for applicability
exactMathematicalFragment.equivalence: DPO diagram squares up to canonical isomorphism under adhesive assumptions
exactMathematicalFragment.composition: pushout along monos, categorical pullbacks, van Kampen property; well-behaved compositional rewriting conditional on admissibility
exactMathematicalFragment.mathPrerequisites: Must work in adhesive C with valid monos/pushout complement; category of posets Pos is explicitly nonadhesive.

sourcePaperRecords.broadPhysicalCategory: Formal graph transformation in mathematics and computation, not an established gravitational theory.
sourcePaperRecords.fineInterpretationBoundary: Because incidence R is a presheaf topos, ambient R is adhesive. The full category of native state-labelled k-ary guards is not proven adhesive, nor DPO match+guards automatically preserve actual Causal Step all states or original T4 83/660 tests.
sourcePaperRecords.candidateNativeMapping: Represent node/edge incidence plus labels in ambient R; attempt guarded DPO rule with fresh node, conditional existing-member bit mutation, keep/consume and offspring creation; prove exact match and composition only under all source-specific constraints.
sourcePaperRecords.mappingStatus: ambient theorem applies; native guarded DPO embedding not constructed/proved

sourcePaperRecords.title: Incidence Hypergraphs: Box Products and the Laplacian
sourcePaperRecords.sourceVersion: arXiv:2007.01842v4 2023-07-12, original PDF of paper submitted 2020
originalMathLocators: PDF index 12 (printed p13) §3.1 Definition 3.1.1 and Theorem 3.1.3: incidence dual G# swaps V and E and s/t, functor involutive.
PDF index 12–15 §3.1 Def 3.1.5 Laplacian product and Theorem 3.1.10 (PDF index 15) natural dual/product isomorphisms (G■H)# ≅ G#■H ≅ G■H#.
PDF index 21–23 §4.2 relates the path evaluation of Laplacian exponential to signed/symmetric graph Laplacian powers; not equivalent to source Carletti k-weighted Laplacian definition.

exactMathematicalFragment.objects: Incidence category R as presheaves; edge/vertex duality; Laplacian monoidal product and exponential.
exactMathematicalFragment.morphisms: Natural incidence dual G#=(E,V,I,t,s); dual action on morphisms; Laplacian product natural isomorphisms
exactMathematicalFragment.equivalence: G## naturally equals/isomorphic G in the ambient category, not native vertex↔hyperedge *physical* equivalence
exactMathematicalFragment.composition: Functorial incidence duality and symmetric monoidal product with stated natural coherences; matrix/paths are derived observers.
exactMathematicalFragment.mathPrerequisites: Ambient incidence presheaves, available loose incidences, specified monoidal product and path evaluation; source oriented-graph sign conventions

sourcePaperRecords.broadPhysicalCategory: Graph combinatorics and Laplacian/network operators; no asserted physical light or gravity identity.
sourcePaperRecords.fineInterpretationBoundary: Duality swaps nodes and hyperedge occurrences in the ambient graph category; the native nodes hold bit/birth states and E occurrences have fired/alive flags, and ranks differ, so native dynamics is NOT dual-invariant. The 'Laplacian' here is source-specific, not Carletti–Fanelli–Nicoletti weighted dyadic K/L by name alone.
sourcePaperRecords.candidateNativeMapping: Try dualization as mathematical presentation comparison for unlabelled incidence, then test loss when restoring native types and guards; not a physical duality.
sourcePaperRecords.mappingStatus: ambient incidence duality genuine exact; full native dynamics not shown to preserve it

sourcePaperRecords.title: Pregeometric Spaces from Wolfram Model Rewriting Systems as Homotopy Types
sourcePaperRecords.sourceVersion: 2024-03-28 original publisher open-access HTML, International Journal of Theoretical Physics 63 article 83; DOI 10.1007/s10773-024-05576-0
originalMathLocators: Original publisher §§2 Definitions 2.1–2.5: model hypergraph and pattern substitution rewrite H1→H2, abstract rewriting system (A,→), multiway state transition graph and event-causal adjacency In(b)∩Out(a)≠∅.
Publisher §4.2 Proposition 4.1 and Definition 4.1: double-category higher homotopy structure after supplementing multiway system with path-homotopy rewrite rules.
Publisher §4.2 Corollary 4.1, Proposition 4.2–4.4: double groupoid, n-fold and ∞-groupoid interpretations explicitly contingent on invertible higher rules and admissibility.
Publisher §5: ∞-topos/spatial/cohesion constructions require subobject classifiers, additional (co)limits/adjoints and topology/cohesion structures; some fiber construction described as future work.

exactMathematicalFragment.objects: Hypergraph rewriting states, multiway legal path category, additional path/path-homotopy rewrites 2-cells; supplementary higher/invertible rules.
exactMathematicalFragment.morphisms: Source state paths concatenate to form category; added 2-morphisms between paths only with additional rewriting rules; invertibility is added for groupoid constructions.
exactMathematicalFragment.equivalence: higher homotopy/localization conditional, not automatically Causal Step equivalence or proof of native 3D.
exactMathematicalFragment.composition: horizontal/vertical path and 2-cell compositions; higher compositions only when prescribed admissible extra homotopy rules.
exactMathematicalFragment.mathPrerequisites: Particular Wolfram model ordered hyperedge convention, rule patterns, separate causal ancestry definition based on source edge In/Out overlap; additional invertible rules/topos/cohesion infrastructure.

sourcePaperRecords.broadPhysicalCategory: Proposed pregeometric origin of spatial structure in physical models (authors' context, no independent physics validation by this extraction).
sourcePaperRecords.fineInterpretationBoundary: Native source-selected Causal Step model has forced new vertices, non-invertible forward actions and bit-sensitive T4 conflict; its full path category cannot be declared ∞-groupoid or cohesive ∞-topos from this paper alone. Source notion of causal network uses produced edge reuse, not necessarily same as our forest of creator node ancestry or operational conflict.
sourcePaperRecords.candidateNativeMapping: Objects: full native states, 1-morphisms: legal finite selected-event sequences with occurrence IDs, 2-morphisms: ONLY pairs of histories for which an explicit admissible 2-cell is defined. Compare original multiway and category construction without adding inverses to native rules.
